description: This article on the Digital Regulation Platform gives governments and other stakeholders guidance on the latest developments in non-geostationary orbit (NGSO) satellite constellations and the regulatory frameworks in place, building on the 2012 report on regulation of global broadband satellite communications. It covers the background and characteristics of NGSO systems, including an estimate of 8,496 active satellites on 1 September 2023 with 90 percent in low Earth orbit, and the policy and regulatory questions for spectrum and orbits, interference-free operation, market access, emerging business models, space traffic management and debris. Producer: the Digital Regulation Platform of ITU and the World Bank, dated 28 March 2024. Coverage: global, with national, regional and international regulatory levels. Access: free web page. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: it is guidance text with dated satellite counts and no dataset. Simulation uses: it explains regulatory constraints on spectrum and market access that shape constellation deployment scenarios. Related records: none linked.
